t: Plan a week of family dinners on a set budget

steps.b: Open ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini and paste this prompt with your details filled in.
steps.p: Plan 7 dinners for [number] people (including [ages of children, if any]) with a total food budget of about [amount] for the week. We shop at [supermarket type, e.g. a big supermarket or a discount store]. Avoid [allergies and dislikes]. Reuse ingredients across meals so nothing is wasted, include at least 2 meat-free dinners, and keep weeknight meals under [30] minutes. example: Mon: Lentil & sweet potato curry (about 4.20). Tue: Leftover curry wraps with salad. Wed: Sausage & bean one-pot... Shopping: Veg - 2 onions, 1kg sweet potato, garlic. Tins - 2 chopped tomatoes, 1 coconut milk. Leftovers: save half the rice for Thursday's egg fried rice.

Tell it which meals were a hit so next week's plan repeats the favourites.

Give me: 1) two or three base recipes I can mix and match; 2) one shopping list by aisle; 3) the prep order step by step; 4) how to store each lunch and which to eat first.

steps.b: Keep the plan and list in your notes app, and note which lunches you enjoyed for next time.

example: Base 1: chickpea, roasted veg & quinoa bowl. Base 2: chicken, brown rice & greens with a peanut-free satay sauce. Prep: 0:00 oven on, veg in; 0:10 grains on... Eat first: chicken bowls Mon-Tue, chickpea bowls Wed-Fri. Keep dressings separate.
tips: For specific nutrition needs, such as diabetes or a medical diet, ask your GP or a registered dietitian rather than relying on AI.

t: Understand a hospital letter in plain English
d: Get a plain-English explanation of medical words in a letter or leaflet, plus questions to ask your care team.
when: When a letter or leaflet is hard to follow

steps.b: Before sharing anything, cover or delete your name, address, date of birth, hospital and NHS or insurance numbers.
Paste the text, or a photo with details covered, into your AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: Please explain this [hospital letter/leaflet] in plain English for someone without medical training: [paste text]. Explain each medical word or abbreviation simply, list any practical things it asks me to do (appointments, preparation, dates), and give me 5 questions I could ask my doctor or nurse. Don't interpret test results or tell me what they mean for my health, and say clearly if something should be checked with my care team.

steps.b: Take your questions to your GP, consultant, nurse or pharmacist. They know your full history and can explain what it means for you.

example: 'Bilateral' means both sides. 'Ultrasound' is a scan using sound waves, it's painless. What to do: drink 1 litre of water an hour before your scan on 4 Dec, don't empty your bladder. Questions: How long will results take? Who will tell me the results?
tips: AI explanations can be wrong or miss context, so always check what matters with your care team.
Health information is sensitive: share only what you need and check the AI tool's privacy settings.

t: Keep your family's health details in one safe place
d: Create one private record of allergies, vaccinations, medicines and appointments for everyone you care for.
when: Set up once, update after appointments

steps.b: Make a Google Docs or Word file stored in your own account, not a shared folder, and turn on two-step verification for that account.
Ask your AI assistant for a structure, then fill in the real details yourself in the document, not in the chat.
steps.p: Create a blank template for a family health record I'll fill in myself. For each person include sections for: allergies and reactions, current medicines (name, dose, who prescribed), vaccinations with dates, ongoing conditions, past operations, GP and dentist contact, upcoming appointments, and notes from recent appointments. Add a short 'emergency summary' box at the top of each person's section. Use headings and tables, with placeholder text only.

steps.h: Fill it in from official records
steps.b: Copy details from red books, vaccination records, prescription labels and your GP surgery's app or patient portal.
Add appointments to Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar and put the appointment notes in the record afterwards.

example: Emergency summary - Leo (7): Allergic to penicillin (rash). Inhaler: blue, as needed. GP: Riverside Surgery. Vaccinations: preschool booster 03/2023. Upcoming: asthma review 12 Jan. Last notes: nurse said to bring the inhaler to every review.
tips: Keep real health details in your own private document, not in AI chats, and be careful who you share it with.
Ask your GP surgery or pharmacist if anything in the record is unclear.

t: Beat desk stiffness with short movement breaks
d: Get a set of two-minute stretches you can do at your desk, with gentle reminders through the working day.
when: During long days at a desk

steps.b: Paste this prompt into your AI assistant.
steps.p: I sit at a desk for about [hours] a day and feel stiff in my [neck/shoulders/back/hips]. Create 4 different 2-minute movement breaks I can do at my desk or next to it, in work clothes, without getting sweaty. For each: 3-4 moves with simple instructions, how long to hold or repeat, and an easier option. Tell me to stop any move that causes pain.

steps.b: Create repeating reminders every 60 to 90 minutes during work hours on your phone or computer, each named after one of the routines.
Link a break to something you already do, like after every video call or each time you refill your water.

example: Break 1 - Neck & shoulders: shoulder rolls x10 back, x10 forward. Slow chin tucks x8. Ear-to-shoulder hold 15 sec each side. Doorway chest stretch 20 sec. Easier: do it all seated.
tips: If pain persists or you have numbness or tingling, see your GP or a physiotherapist.

t: See your workout progress with a weekly review
d: Log workouts with a quick form, keep them in a sheet and get an automatic weekly progress summary by email.
when: Log after each workout, review weekly

steps.b: Create a Google Forms form with questions for date, workout type, duration, main exercises and weights or distance, effort out of 10 and a note. Link it to a Google Sheet.

steps.h: Put the form on your home screen
steps.b: Open the form link on your phone and add it to your home screen, so logging takes under a minute after each session.

If your AI assistant offers scheduled tasks or can read your Google Drive (some plans include this), schedule a weekly task with this prompt. Otherwise, set a Sunday reminder and paste the last week's rows yourself.
steps.p: Review my workout log for the last 7 days: [paste rows or point to the sheet]. Compare with the previous 4 weeks. Give me: total sessions and minutes, any lifts or distances that improved, how my effort scores are trending, whether I'm doing too much or too little based on my goal of [goal], and one suggestion for next week. Use a short table and 3 bullet points. Don't give medical advice.

steps.b: Have the summary sent to your email, or copy it into an email draft to yourself, so you have a record of each week.

example: Week 45: 4 sessions, 185 mins (up 20). Squat 5x5 at 52.5kg (+2.5kg). 5k run 31:10 (down from 32:05). Effort average 7.5 - a little high for 4 days. Next week: make Thursday an easy walk or rest day.
tips: Keep the sheet private; even workout data can be personal.
If you have pain or a health condition, talk to a GP or qualified trainer before increasing load.

t: Check in with yourself through a short weekly journal
d: Use a few gentle questions each week to notice your mood, what helped and what drained you, with a calm summary.
when: Once a week, at a quiet moment

steps.b: Paste this prompt into your AI assistant to get a set of questions you'll reuse each week.
steps.p: Give me 6 gentle weekly reflection questions for a personal journal. Cover: mood this week from 1 to 10, what gave me energy, what drained me, one thing I'm proud of, how I looked after myself, and one small thing I'd like to do differently next week. Keep the wording warm and simple. After I answer, summarise my answers kindly in 3 sentences and suggest one small, realistic self-care action. Don't give medical or therapy advice.

steps.b: Copy the questions into a weekly note and write your answers there, adding the date.
Every month or so, read back through your notes, or paste them into the assistant and ask what's changed.

example: Week of 3 Nov - Mood: 6/10. Energy: Saturday walk with Jo, early night Tuesday. Drained: late emails. Proud: said no to an extra shift. Next week: no emails after 8pm. Summary: a steady week, with rest making a clear difference.
tips: If you're struggling, feel low most days or think about harming yourself, talk to your GP or contact a local crisis line or emergency services straight away.
Your journal is private: keep it in a note only you can open.

actions.detail: Send the weekly check-in questions

t: Make sense of your fitness tracker's weekly numbers
d: Turn your watch or phone's weekly steps, sleep and activity stats into a short, plain-English summary and one goal.
when: Once a week

steps.b: Open your fitness or health app's weekly view and take screenshots of steps, active minutes and sleep, or note the numbers down.
Attach the screenshots to your AI assistant with this prompt.
steps.p: Here are my weekly fitness tracker stats: [attach screenshots or paste numbers]. My goal is [e.g. move more, sleep better]. In plain English: 1) summarise the week in 3 sentences; 2) compare with general guidance for adults, such as around 150 minutes of moderate activity a week; 3) point out my best and hardest days; 4) suggest one small, specific goal for next week. Don't make health judgements from the data.

steps.b: Put the goal in your reminders app, for example 'Walk to the shop on Tuesday and Thursday'.

example: This week: 41,200 steps (about 5,900 a day), 96 active minutes, average 6h 40m sleep. Best day: Saturday (11,800 steps). Hardest: Wednesday. You're about two-thirds of the way to 150 active minutes. Goal: a 20-minute walk on 3 weekdays.
tips: Trackers are estimates; if your numbers worry you, such as heart rate alerts, talk to your GP rather than relying on AI.

t: Share caring for a parent with your siblings
d: Keep one shared calendar and running note of a parent's appointments, medicines and who's doing what each week.
when: Set up once, update weekly

steps.b: Talk to your parent first about what they're happy to share, and with whom. It's their information.
Make a new Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar just for their care, and share it with the family. Add appointments, prescription collection days and visits, with who is going.
Create a shared Google Docs or Word file for updates after each appointment and visit, so everyone knows the latest.
Each week, paste the latest notes (using first names only) into your AI assistant with this prompt and share the result in the family WhatsApp group.
steps.p: Here are this week's care notes for my parent: [paste notes, first names only]. Write a short, kind family update with: how they're doing, appointments and outcomes this week, anything that's changed, next week's calendar, and who's covering what. Then list any gaps where no one is down to help. Don't add any medical advice or interpretation.

example: Mum's week: in good spirits, walked to the shop twice. Tuesday: GP review, blood pressure tablets unchanged. Next week: Thu 10:30 eye clinic (Raj driving), prescription pick-up Fri (Sarah). Gap: no one free for Sunday lunch visit yet.
tips: Keep the calendar and notes shared only with close family, and check your parent is comfortable with what's written.
Questions about treatment should go to their GP or care team.

t: Stay on top of repeat prescriptions and check-ups
d: Gather health admin emails in one label, track repeat prescriptions in a sheet and get reminders before you run out.
when: Set up once, runs every month

steps.b: In Gmail's settings, under Filters, create filters for emails from your GP surgery, pharmacy, dentist and optician that apply a 'Health admin' label. Outlook users can do this with rules.
Create a Google Sheets or Excel file with columns: Medicine (or a nickname), Quantity supplied, Date collected, Days it lasts, Reorder by, Notes.
Paste the rows into your AI assistant with this prompt and copy the dates back into the sheet. You can also use a simple formula: date collected plus days it lasts, minus 7.
steps.p: Here are my repeat prescriptions: [paste rows using nicknames]. For each, work out the date I'll run out and a 'reorder by' date [7] days before, allowing for weekends. Then list my upcoming routine check-ups from these notes: [e.g. dentist every 6 months, last visit 3 May; eye test every 2 years, last March 2025]. Output one table sorted by date. Don't comment on the medicines themselves.

steps.b: Create a Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar event for each reorder date and check-up, set to repeat where it makes sense.
Once a month, check the 'Health admin' label for anything new and update the sheet.

example: Inhaler (blue): collected 1 Nov, lasts 30 days, reorder by 24 Nov. Tablets (morning): collected 5 Nov, 56 days, reorder by 23 Dec. Dentist check-up due 3 Nov - overdue, book now. Eye test due March 2027.
tips: Use nicknames for medicines in AI tools if you'd rather not share them, and keep the sheet private.
Follow your GP or pharmacist's advice on how early to reorder; some surgeries need several working days.
